meta.title: Embedded wiring
meta.description: A workspace can hold several wiring netlists: every hardware/wiring.json is one project and travels with the directory it lives in. The page scans the workspace, lists the projects, and counts the boards; a board shows its pins in the two columns it really has, you drag a part by its title, drag from one pin dot to another to wire them, and click a wire to rename it or set its protocol and pull-up; 「一键整理」 lays the parts out by their wires and splits each module's pins between the two edges their wires leave towards. It validates what would actually fail on the bench — missing common ground, 5V on a 3.3V pin, two outputs on one net, strapping pins, I2C without pull-ups — and the agent reads and changes the same netlist through the hardware_map tool (defaulting to the project nearest the session directory), optionally as suggestions you apply on the page. Send the agent a photo of a module and it adds a part with its pin table marked unverified, which you confirm on the page once you have checked the silkscreen. Open it from the 接线 row in the left sidebar. It is a connection record, not an electrical check: it cannot see current, wire gauge, or EMI.
